title: Hundesteuer-Atlas: der Steuersatz jeder Gemeinde aus der eigenen Satzung
pitch: For dog owners and people about to get a dog in Germany: one page per municipality with the current and announced dog-tax rates (first and second dog, listed or dangerous dogs), reductions and exemptions, and a link to the bylaw, extracted from municipal bylaws and refreshed every budget season.

evidence.note: Paderborn raises the first-dog tax from 72 to 120 EUR from January 2027 (unchanged since 2000). An online petition against it ran until 11 November.
The best calculator found covers only 33 large cities (checked 2026-10-17) and lists 2027 rates for Hamburg, Munich and Nuremberg. Other municipalities are not covered.

competitors.gap: Compares 14 large cities, according to the search result (not opened).

competitors.gap: NRW only, PDF tables published once a year, nothing per municipality.

trigger.what: A wave of dog-tax increases for 2027 decided in the Oct-Nov 2026 budget sessions (e.g. Paderborn 72 to 120 EUR from January 2027, final council vote 2026-11-12). This recurs every year.

window: Standing gap with a yearly peak: rates change on January 1 after autumn budget votes. The only per-municipality data sets are hand-made and partial (33 or 14 big cities, NRW-only PDFs), and nobody covers the roughly 10,000 smaller municipalities, where a search returns only insurers' generic pages.
monetizationIdea: Affiliate links to dog liability insurance comparisons (insurers such as Allianz and ARAG run dog-tax pages for exactly this audience), plus display ads. A municipality's page is visited at the moment someone registers a new dog.
risks: Wrong rate shown; always show source, date checked and a link to the bylaw
Do not copy the Bund der Steuerzahler tables (possible database right); extract from the bylaws themselves
demandNote: The dated items (Paderborn 2026-11-05, plus Black Forest towns raising 2027 rates in search results) show the topic is live and the data changes now, but I found no dated request for a lookup tool.
